title: Lacson questions VP camp’s ‘honest mistake’ claim
summary: Sen. Panfilo Lacson yesterday cast doubt that Vice President made an “honest mistake” in declaring shares in GenCorp Industries in her statement of assets, liabilities and net worth.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Panfilo Lacson yesterday cast doubt that Vice President made an “honest mistake” in declaring shares in GenCorp Industries in her statement of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN).
Lacson was reacting to former chief presidential legal counsel Salvador Panelo, who made the remark in defense of the Vice President.
On X, Lacson tweeted that the Vice President’s “honest mistake” in declaring GenCorp shares despite its absence in the incorporation papers is a “double-edged sword.”

“Its meaning depends on the state of mind and intent of the person behind it. It can be an inadvertent slip that exposes the truth, or a genuine blind spot that mistakes falsehood for reality. Ultimately, only the person responsible can say which is which,” he added.

The Senate impeachment court is looking at the impeachment article on Duterte’s alleged unexplained and hidden wealth and for having business interests despite a constitutional ban during a Vice President’s tenure.
GenCorp is declared in her SALN as among the firms where the Vice President had shares. However, GenCorp’s corporate records did not identify her as an officer or shareholder.

Another allegation against the Vice President was her receipt from 2022 to 2025 of up to P2.14 million in “return of capital” or earnings from her “loose investment” of just P46,875 at a Jollibee branch in Davao City.
Meanwhile, an impeachment verdict may come as early as December if the defense completes its remaining eight to 10 witnesses within the next few weeks, the prosecution said.

House prosecutor and Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon said the defense could finish presenting its evidence by the end of November or during the first week of December, if they only have around eight to 10 witnesses to present. — Daphne Galvez
